_comment: Dependent-suite failures we have already diagnosed as flaky rather than caused
by a nodus-lang change. `tools/check_dependent_suites.py` uses this only to
CLASSIFY a red result -- never to pass one.
That distinction is the whole design. A known-flaky test failing is not evidence
the release is fine; it is evidence that this particular red needs a serial
re-run rather than a bisect. So the gate still exits non-zero (3 instead of 1)
and still says what to do. Letting a listed test pass the gate would rebuild
're-run until green' one level up, which is the failure this whole process
`match` is a substring of the pytest node id (`path::Class::test`), so naming a
file covers every test in it. Keep entries as narrow as the evidence supports.
To add one: diagnose it first. `why` should say what was actually established,
not what was assumed -- an entry whose reason is 'seems flaky' is a way to lose

nodus-mcp.why: Two tests in this file bind ports and fail when another suite holds them. Documented in CLAUDE.md as a pre-existing race, not a code bug. What is established: a serial full-suite run is green (2/2 at v5.4.0, 363 tests each). What is NOT established is that they pass individually -- running the file alone failed 1 in 7 at v5.4.0. So the check that discriminates a flake from a regression here is a serial FULL-SUITE re-run; a green single-file run is weaker evidence than it looks, and a red one is not yet a finding.
nodus-mcp.recorded: 2026-08-20, during the v5.1.0 Gate 10 run, where this fired while a clean-venv install and probe suite ran alongside it. Three serial re-runs were green. Re-examined 2026-08-25 at v5.4.0 Gate 10a, twelve runs: 2/2 full serial suites green, the file alone 6/7, the single test 3/3, and 3/3 green against the installed 5.0.0 -- which is why the 'pass individually' half of the original reason was withdrawn above.
